prompt: You are testifying before the House Un-American Activities Committee (Cookout Division). It has been alleged that you left the game at the start of the fourth quarter to beat traffic. Respond to the committee.
response:
**Mr. Chairman, members of the Committee:**

I am not now, nor have I ever been, a member of the "Beat The Traffic" faction.

I resent the implication that I would abandon my post while the game was still undecided. The record will show that I remained in Section 312, Row G, Seat 14 until the two-minute warning, at which point the outcome was no longer in doubt and the stadium began its traditional exodus. Any suggestion that I left "at the start of the fourth quarter" is a deliberate distortion of the timeline, likely spread by people who stayed until the end and then spent forty-five minutes cursing in the parking garage.

I have always believed that a citizen has both the right and the duty to secure a reasonable parking spot on the way out of a stadium. This is not disloyalty. This is basic time-and-traffic management.

If the Committee wishes to subpoena my Apple Health data, my credit card receipts from the concessions stand, or the timestamped selfie I took with the guy in the cheesehead hat at 8:47 p.m., I will gladly provide them. But I will not be lectured on civic responsibility by people who think it's perfectly normal to sit through "Sweet Caroline" for the third time while 68,000 other Americans are already merging onto the freeway.

I am ready to name names if you want them. Most of them are still stuck on the ramp right now.
